answer: When k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, the protocol aggregates pairwise links, so the penalty grows as O(k²), not merely with the number of signers. Slashed escrow and asymmetric depreciation compound the loss: once detection confirms coordinated control, each additional linked identity raises the multiplier, making swarm-wide capital loss exponential. A canyon of aliases offers no shelter; each pearl of evidence and quill-signed conflicting message can strengthen the correlation proof.
